newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan says portfolio oil investors must wait.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan says portfolio oil investors must wait.

text.p: Government stakes in Kazakh oil companies should not be offered to portfolio investors for at least another year to give them time to appreciate, the head of Kazakhstan's state Kazakh Oil said on Monday.

"It is too early to bring the so-called "blue chips" to the stock market," Nurlan Balgimbayev told a news conference. "We should wait for these (oil) companies to become stronger, and within one or two years, their shares will be of greater value."
Kazakh Oil, set up under presidential decree in March, manages state-owned shares -- many of them minority stakes -- in oil companies.
Kazakhstan has offered significant stakes in its major energy enterprises to single strategic investors, but it has not offered shares to portfolio investors.

But the government, which plans to complete sell-offs of oil companies to strategic investors by July 1, eventually aims to offer the remaining state stakes to portfolio investors to help create a corporate shares market.
Energy-rich Kazakhstan, luring strategic investors to the Central Asian state's giant natural resources, has favoured management contracts over a limited period of time.
Balgimbayev said that if state-run stakes in local oil companies were offered to portfolio investors, Kazakh Oil would compete for these stakes alongside other bidders.
"Kazakhstan is an oil state, and imagine that it would not have oil companies of its own. This is a nonsense," he told reporters.

Kazakhstan cherishes ambitious plans to boost its oil output to 170 million tonnes (3.4 million barrels per day) in 2010 from 26.5 million (530,000 bpd) this year, and to become, by current production levels, the world's sixth largest crude oil producer.
